atoms.span: EA-PREDICTION-INDEX-01 is a large-scale, source-quoted register of predictions
It was authored by Lee Sharks and deposited in Alexanarch as deposit #1684 (AXN:06FA) on 18 October 2026.
The document's own description is important: it presents the index as a record of claims, not as a judgment that those claims are true or that predictions have been fulfilled.
priority claims made throughout the Crimson Hexagonal Archive
Its central purpose is to make the archive's predictive content identifiable, traceable, organized, and eventually testable.
That distinction prevents a reader-created interpretation from being misrepresented as the author's original test.
The stable claim identifiers are especially important. A claim's subject page or grouping can change when the index is rebuilt, but its permanent claim route remains stable.
Build identity, provenance, hashes, and history

observations.notes: Eight of eleven atoms present. Framework absent: operative semiotics, operativesemiotics.org, the prospective kernel and The Negative of the Negative (#1611) are never named; the subject pages appear only as link labels. Lineage absent: prediction-registry.json and the prediction ledger, the index's predecessor and its resolution layer, are not mentioned. Deposit chain absent: the build id is given and builds.json is glossed 'Build identity, provenance, hashes, and history', but the deposit's anchoring of one build and the index's supersession of the earlier registry's counts are not. Claim boundary present (five tiers at their counts, earliest registration, four dates, confirmation records with no verdict, priority membership open, recall on one sample of forty); the record's 'so the figure is an upper bound' is not carried. Commitments present (no verdict, the source's falsifier kept apart from the reader's, quotations checked by script, the safeguard on speculative specifications); §4.1, descriptions naming whose claim each is, and the licence are absent.
